solution:
Since \(\tan A=\cot B\iff A+B=n\pi+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\), the equation gives \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\sin\theta+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\cos\theta=n\pi+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\), i.e. \(\sin\theta+\cos\theta=2n+1\).

Because \(|\sin\theta+\cos\theta|\le\sqrt2\), the only admissible odd integers are \(\pm1\).

\(\sin\theta+\cos\theta=1\Rightarrow\theta=2r\pi\) or \(\theta=2r\pi+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\); the second is INADMISSIBLE, since \(\tan\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\sin\theta\right)=\tan\dfrac{\pi}{2}\) is undefined there.

\(\sin\theta+\cos\theta=-1\Rightarrow\theta=2r\pi+\pi\) or \(\theta=2r\pi-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\); the first IS admissible — at \(\theta=\pi\), \(\tan\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\sin\pi\right)=\tan 0=0\) and \(\cot\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\cos\pi\right)=\cot\!\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)=0\) — while the second is again undefined.

So the complete solution set is \(\theta=r\pi\), \(r\in Z\), i.e. every integer multiple of \(\pi\), not merely the even ones. Option B, \(\theta=2r\pi\), lists only valid solutions but MISSES the odd multiples, so it is incomplete; option A and hence option C contain the inadmissible \(\pi/2\) branch. No listed option is the full solution set. Matches option D: None.

(Verified numerically: \(\theta=0,\pi,2\pi\) all satisfy the equation, while \(\theta=\pi/2\) and \(3\pi/2\) leave both sides undefined.)
